A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the presence of fluoride ion in aluminophosphate synthesis using ionic liquids and amines is essential to produce the same frameworks as the amines, while in the absence of fluoride ion the frameworks are not related.
the ionic liquid precursory route to aluminophosphate materials can be very successful and can be used to produce materials with a wide range of structures and properties.

the presence of fluoride in the synthesis is important for the formation of the same aluminophosphates using the same ionic liquids as solvent and template as the parent amines, while in the absence of fluoride ions the products formed are not related to each other.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ionic liquids are useful solvents and templates for aluminophosphate synthesis.
ionic liquids are not necessary for the synthesis of aluminophosphates and their use in synthesis is limited by the fact that they are not good solvents for phosphoric acid.
ionic liquid precursers can be used to produce zeolites with a range of framework topologies.
